To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
European Works Councils (EWCs) are an important new institution in transnational corporations, but they do not yet work in a way that facilitates the development of transnational trade unions.

EWCs have been established as a new transnational form of industrial relations, which has been used to a certain extent by trade unions to improve the situation of workers in multinational corporations, but which has not yet been fully exploited by trade unions to develop new forms of transnational solidarity and to improve the bargaining power of workers.
EWCs can be a powerful tool in the hands of unions, but only if unions are prepared to invest in their development.
